item.title: 12 leaders of APEC economies to attend APEC CEO Summit 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
SHENZHEN, Nov. 15 (Xinhua) -- Twelve leaders of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies will attend the APEC CEO Summit 2026, which is scheduled to be held from Nov. 17 to 18 in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) said Sunday.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, along with leaders from APEC economies Australia, Canada, Chile, China's Hong Kong, Indonesia, the Republic of Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, Russia, Thailand and Vietnam, will attend the summit and deliver speeches or remarks, or participate in panel discussions, said Li Qingshuang, vice chairperson of the CCPIT, at a press conference.

item.title: Shenzhen ready to host APEC 2026, officials say
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
A press briefing for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week was held in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, southern China, on November 14, 2026. /Xinhua
Shenzhen is officially ready to host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting on November 18 and 19, local officials confirmed on Saturday.
Organizers have upgraded key venues, conducted rehearsals, and infused the event with green practices, digital tech and traditional Lingnan culture, Wang Xi, deputy head of the provincial preparatory leading group, said.
To make it more convenient for visiting delegates, the city in south China's Guangdong Province has set up dedicated fast-track channels at nine sea, land, air and rail ports, over 100,000 standardized foreign-language signs, and more than 7,000 AI translation devices at key locations. Taxis will play bilingual announcements, the metro will accept contactless overseas bank cards, and over 3,000 ATMs will be ready for cash withdrawals with foreign bank cards.
Additionally, currency exchanges will be possible at some 1,600 bank branches and tax refunds in 3,160 shops, including more than 1,000 offering instant refunds.
During the meeting week, Guangdong is offering 218 visitor sites and 43 travel routes, including two showcase routes in Shenzhen.
Shenzhen Mayor Li Yun said the city has boosted transport, power, communications and hotel services while minimizing disruptions to residents' daily lives.
Meanwhile, the city's economy is booming. Shenzhen has become the first city on the Chinese mainland to top 5 trillion yuan (about $ 744.6 billion) in foreign trade. Customs data shows imports and exports hitting 5.25 trillion yuan in the first 10 months of the year, a 40.9% jump year on year. Exports rose 19.7% to 2.71 trillion yuan, while imports surged 73.7% to 2.54 trillion yuan.

item.title: China, U.S. hold first meeting of trade council under economic, trade consultation mechanism
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
BEIJING, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- China and the United States held the first meeting of the trade council under the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism via video link on Friday, China's Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday.
Guided by the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, the meeting focused on implementing the outcomes of previous rounds of bilateral economic and trade consultations.
The two sides had a candid, in-depth and constructive exchange on tariffs, the reciprocal tariff reduction arrangement covering about 30 billion U.S. dollars worth of each other's goods, agricultural trade and other issues of mutual concern.
Both sides will continue to strengthen communication through the trade council, work to resolve their respective economic and trade concerns, further expand cooperation and shorten the list of issues, so as to help build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, the ministry noted.
In May 2026, China and the United States agreed to establish a trade council to address their respective concerns in trade cooperation.
The two sides held the eighth round of their economic and trade consultations in New York and Washington, D.C. from Sept. 20 to 23. During the consultations, they agreed to reduce tariffs on about 30 billion U.S. dollars worth of goods imported from each other on a reciprocal basis, with tariffs on around 90 percent of the covered products to be lowered to most-favored-nation rates.

item.title: "China, Thailand as close as one family" a unique advantage of bilateral ties, says Chinese premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Thai King Maha Vajiralongkorn in Bangkok, Thailand, Nov. 14, 2026. (Xinhua)
BANGKOK, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Saturday that "China and Thailand are as close as one family" is a unique advantage of bilateral relations, as reflected in the practical achievements across various fields.
Li made the remarks during his meeting with Thai King Maha Vajiralongkorn in Bangkok.
Conveying cordial greetings from Chinese President Xi Jinping to the king, Li said that during the king's state visit to China last year, Xi held talks with him, and the two sides reached important consensus on advancing the building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future.
China appreciates that the Thai royal family has long attached great importance to and remained committed to promoting China-Thailand friendship, Li said.
He noted that the continued growth of China-Thailand economic and trade cooperation despite headwinds is particularly commendable amid the current turbulent international situation.
Li said that China stands ready to work with Thailand, under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, to maintain close exchanges, expand cooperation in investment, technological innovation, new energy vehicles and other areas, deepen people-to-people exchanges, and promote economic and social development in both countries for the greater well-being of their peoples.
The Thai king asked Li to convey his sincere greetings and best wishes to President Xi. Recalling his state visit to China last year, the king said that the successful meeting with Xi was fruitful and remained fresh in his memory.
Li's official visit to Thailand would help further consolidate the traditional friendship between Thailand and China and deepen practical cooperation between the two countries, the king said.

item.title: How Chinese innovation drives shared growth from Shenzhen to Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
* Shenzhen offers a snapshot of this vibrant high-tech trade story. Total R&D spending in the city grew at an average annual rate of 12.9 percent from 2020 to 2024, and R&D intensity reached 6.67 percent, the highest among Chinese cities. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou innovation cluster has also topped the Global Innovation Index rankings.
* Cooperation between Shenzhen and its Asia-Pacific partners advances along a well-defined track, featuring manufacturing, research and talent development, and the practical application of technology, said Chen Jiaxi, vice president of the Shenzhen Reform and Opening Up Executive Leadership Academy.
* "The Shenzhen meeting will send a clear signal: China's commitment to high-standard opening up, to sharing opportunities with the Asia-Pacific, and to multilateralism remains firm," said Chen, who is also a professor at Shenzhen University.
SHENZHEN, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- From a battery anode materials plant built from scratch in Indonesia to a surgical robot in a Kuala Lumpur operating room and solar panels atop a century-old Thai university, companies from China's southern tech hub of Shenzhen have established a presence across the Asia-Pacific region.
Next week, as Shenzhen in Guangdong Province hosts the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the innovative, collaborative approach that Shenzhen embodies will take center stage.
The numbers are significant. China's goods trade with other APEC members reached 26.29 trillion yuan (about 3.9 trillion U.S. dollars) in 2025, or nearly 60 percent of its total foreign trade, according to the General Administration of Customs. High-tech goods are an increasingly strong link: China's exports of such products to other APEC members rose 8.1 percent to 4.63 trillion yuan in 2025.
A drone photo shows an exterior view of PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material (PT BTR) at Kendal Industrial Park in Central Java province, Indonesia, Aug. 7, 2024. (Xinhua/Xu Qin)
BUILDING LOCALLY
BTR New Material Group (BTR), a Shenzhen-based battery materials maker, opened an anode material plant in Indonesia's Kendal Industrial Park in August 2024 -- the first overseas anode production base built by a Chinese company in the sector, said He Xueqin, the group's chairman.
Before this plant, Indonesia had no lithium-ion battery anode manufacturing industry at all, He said. Then-Indonesian president Joko Widodo attended the opening, saying it brought the country a step closer to building an electric-vehicle ecosystem, the Economic Daily reported at the time.
Two years on, a second phase is in full operation, doubling annual capacity to 160,000 tonnes. The Indonesian subsidiary's revenue jumped 161 percent year on year to 1.71 billion yuan in the first half of 2026, supplying battery makers in Japan, the Republic of Korea, Europe and the United States.
Before the plant, Indonesia had already built a cathode materials industry from its nickel resources, and BTR added the anode link. "By 2026, separator and electrolyte production has also landed in Indonesia, completing the four main battery materials and laying a solid foundation for the electric-vehicle ecosystem," He said.
The deeper shift is what BTR calls "chain-style overseas expansion," with the company having urged its strategic suppliers to move with it, helping them with local research, assessment and site selection. Packaging and crucible suppliers have already set up operations in Indonesia.
Shenzhen SED Industry Co., Ltd. (SED), a subsidiary of China Electronics Corporation, is exporting plant-building capability itself. For an optical module project in Thailand, its design team analyzed years of local climate data rather than copying domestic designs, adding safeguards against heat and humidity in everything from equipment selection to insulation and cleanroom airtightness.
At an electronics plant in Thailand's 304 Industrial Park, SED applied digital technology across design, construction and operations. Construction clashes fell by more than 95 percent, accidents by over 80 percent, and the plant went from blueprint to completion in just 270 days.
The company now has more than 500 staff and over 1,300 overseas supply chain partners across APEC economies including Thailand, Vietnam and Malaysia, SED said.
Staff members patrol at a plant of Shenzhen SED Industry Co., Ltd. (SED), a subsidiary of China Electronics Corporation, in Thailand in March 2025. (China Electronics Corporation/Handout via Xinhua)
RESEARCH AND TALENT
New plants need people who can run, maintain and improve them. Shenzhen's ties with the region are therefore extending beyond production lines into laboratories and classrooms.
As of March 2026, BGI Group, a Shenzhen-based life science and genomics organization, had jointly trained students with more than 80 universities at home and abroad, including Chulalongkorn University and Mahidol University in Thailand, the University of Indonesia and the University of Malaya. These programs involved 4,490 students in total, 2,503 of them at master's or doctoral level.
Such training is tied to research. With Chulalongkorn University, BGI is working on population aging, gut microbiome studies and thalassemia. In Indonesia, BGI signed an agreement in September 2026 with the health ministry's center for biomedical and health genomics to support the Biomedical and Genome Science Initiative, the country's first national genome program, covering joint research, platform development and local training.
BGI describes its approach as "using projects to build disciplines, industries and talent." Since 2018, BGI has run 13 national-level training programs for more than 360 mid- and senior-level biotech professionals from Belt and Road partner countries, almost 60 percent of them from APEC members, and several alumni have become senior public health officials at home, the company said.
Surgeons perform a robot-assisted surgery in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in September 2026. (Yuanhua Tech/Handout via Xinhua)
TECHNOLOGY ON THE GROUND
The ultimate test of sci-tech cooperation is whether it can serve local needs and improve everyday life. In a Kuala Lumpur operating room, orthopaedic surgeon Rajiv Rampal guided a Shenzhen-developed robot through a hip replacement. The machine, developed by Shenzhen-based Yuanhua Robotics, Perception and AI Technologies Ltd. (Yuanhua Tech) and manufactured in Hong Kong, completed its first Malaysian operation in July and had performed 21 procedures by early September.
Unlike many surgical robots that are tied to specific implant brands, the Shenzhen robot runs on an open platform: all 21 operations used international-brand implants familiar to local doctors.
AI algorithms plan for different implant brands, achieving sub-millimeter placement without changing surgeons' routines. "Let the machine adapt to the doctor, not the doctor to the machine," a Yuanhua Tech official said.
Shenzhen's rapid technological innovation, coupled with Hong Kong's international quality control standards, gives Malaysia access to cutting-edge medical technology, an official with the Malaysian Chinese-language daily Kwong Wah Yit Poh said.
At century-old Mahidol University in Thailand, 41 campus buildings are topped with solar panels. Huawei describes the project as the Asia-Pacific's largest single-site commercial and industrial solar-plus-storage system.
This project serves a national goal. Thailand announced at the COP26 climate summit in 2021 that it would achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, and has encouraged rooftop solar via incentives and tighter safety standards.
The university chose Huawei's smart photovoltaic solution: 15 megawatts of solar capacity, 600 kilowatt-hours of storage and optimisers, which is expected to save around 2.3 million U.S. dollars a year and cut carbon emissions by 11,000 tonnes. The optimisers allow more panels across the 41 rooftops and lift power output by 10 percent, while the storage provides backup power.
The campus is part of a wider footprint. By early 2025, Huawei's digital power business had served over 1,000 Thai enterprises and installed 6 gigawatts of solar inverters, helping generate more than 6 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity and cut carbon dioxide emissions by more than 5 million tonnes, said Yu Junxiang, an official with Huawei's arm in Thailand.
Taken together, Chen said, these cases show how Shenzhen, an urban test case for Chinese modernization, can serve a region: openness breeds cooperation and innovation drives shared growth, offering Asia-Pacific economies a viable path to build consensus, narrow development gaps and achieve shared prosperity.

item.title: China's railway network handles record 4.13 billion passenger trips in first 10 months of 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
Arriving passengers are pictured at Nanjing Railway Station in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province, Oct. 7, 2026. (Photo by Su Yang/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's railway network handled 4.13 billion passenger trips in the first 10 months of the year, up 4.7 percent year on year and the highest for the period on record, China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway) said on Saturday.
The rise reflects increased capacity, improved services and stronger support for tourism and international passenger services.
During the January-October period, the railway operator ran an average of 11,670 passenger trains per day, up 5 percent year on year, according to the company.
Both passenger trips and passenger transport capacity hit single-day records on Oct. 1, the first day of the National Day holiday, with 25.2 million passenger trips recorded and 14,885 trains operated.
Beyond regular passenger services, railway authorities have been promoting the integration of rail and tourism. In the first 10 months of 2026, 3,236 dedicated tourism trains were operated, while an additional 1,084 special trains were arranged for concerts, sports events, exhibitions and study tours.
These efforts are part of a broader drive to stimulate service consumption and support local economies along rail corridors.
Cross-border passenger services also grew strongly in the period. The Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong high-speed railway carried 29.23 million cross-border passengers, up 11 percent year on year, while the China-Laos Railway handled 289,000 cross-border passengers, up 33 percent.
China's railways also saw a surge in foreign visitors. A total of 22.52 million foreign passenger trips were made on the national rail network in the first 10 months of 2026, up 32.9 percent year on year, as more international travelers opted to "tour China by train."
Official data showed that by the end of 2025, the country's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, including more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail.
China's high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, featuring eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. Once complete, the network will connect major cities, city clusters and key economic zones across the country.

item.title: China's independently developed 10-tonne electric aircraft completes first piloted flight
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
This photo taken on Nov. 14, 2026 shows the 10-tonne electric commercial aircraft CE-25A during its maiden piloted flight in Binzhou, east China's Shandong Province. China's independently developed 10-tonne electric commercial aircraft CE-25A completed its maiden piloted flight on Saturday, according to the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC). The aircraft carried two pilots and one flight-test engineer during the flight in Binzhou, east China's Shandong Province. The CE-25A is COMAC's first electric commercial aircraft. Designed mainly for intercity commercial flights, it can carry 19 passengers and has a maximum takeoff weight of 10 tonnes. It has a cruising speed of 300 km per hour, a cruising altitude of 2,400 meters and a range of 400 km. (Photo by Wang Jiliang/Xinhua)
SHANGHAI, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's independently developed 10-tonne electric commercial aircraft CE-25A completed its maiden piloted flight on Saturday, according to the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC).
The aircraft carried two pilots and one flight-test engineer during the flight in Binzhou, east China's Shandong Province. The aircraft operated normally, and all performance indicators met expectations, COMAC said.
The aircraft completed its first unmanned autonomous flight on Feb. 2 this year.
Developed jointly by COMAC, Chinese battery maker CATL, Shanghai Jiao Tong University and other partners, the CE-25A has completed 19 unmanned autonomous flight validations.
The Civil Aviation Administration of China has accepted COMAC's application for a type certificate.

item.title: How Xi's three visits to Shenzhen show China's commitment to reform and opening up
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to attend the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, in south China's Guangdong Province, marking his fourth visit to the birthplace of the country's market-based reforms.
Selected in the late 1970s as a testing ground for China's transition to a more open and market-driven economy, Shenzhen benefited from its proximity to Hong Kong and Macao and its access to maritime trade routes. It has since transformed from a small fishing village into a key driver of China's economic development.
Over the years, Xi has made three visits to Shenzhen. Though each of his visits came at a different stage of the city's and the nation's development, they shared a common thread: China's commitment to pressing ahead with reform and opening up.
Chinese President Xi Jinping places a floral tribute at the bronze statue of Deng Xiaoping in Lianhuashan Park, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, China, on October 14, 2012. /Xinhua
2012: the first inspection tour
Spearheaded by former Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, reform and opening up marked a watershed moment that fundamentally reshaped China's economic and social fabric.
Launched in December 1978, the policy steered the country away from a centrally planned economy toward a market-oriented system, unleashing entrepreneurial energy and igniting a nationwide economic boom.
Much has been achieved. In 1978, China's gross domestic product (GDP) was 367.9 billion yuan, or $149.5 billion, according to World Bank data, which is also cited by the National Bureau of Statistics of China. In just under 50 years, China has developed into the world's second-largest economy, with its GDP reaching 140.19 trillion yuan ($20.4 trillion).
Recognizing the role of reform and opening up in driving this transformation, Xi has repeatedly emphasized the need to uphold and carry forward its legacy. In December 2012, just a month after Xi became the general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, he chose Shenzhen as the first stop of his inspection tour.
During this visit, Xi laid a floral tribute at the bronze statue of Deng Xiaoping in Lianhuashan Park and planted a banyan tree, a symbol of vitality and resilience, underscoring China's dedication to economic reform and determination to navigate any headwinds along the way.
Reaffirming his resolve to stay the course, Xi said, "The decision to launch reform and opening up was right. We must keep to this correct path." He added, "We must stay unwavering on the road to the prosperity of the nation and the people."
Chinese President Xi Jinping visits an exhibition on Guangdong's 40 years of development since the country's reform and opening up, at a museum in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, October 24, 2018. /Xinhua
2018: 40th anniversary of reform and opening up
In October 2018, Xi returned to Shenzhen as the nation marked the 40th anniversary of its reform and opening up, a trip that signaled continued commitment to the policy and an emphasis on greater integration with the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA).
"I come to visit Shenzhen as it marks the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up to tell the world that China will not stop its reform and opening up. China will certainly deliver a bigger miracle that draws worldwide attention," he said.
During his visit, Xi urged the city to deepen cooperation with neighboring Hong Kong to play a bigger role in building the Belt and Road, to advance the development of the GBA, and to participate in international cooperation at higher levels.
In the wake of the visit, China issued the Outline Development Plan for the GBA as well as guidelines to build Shenzhen into a pilot demonstration area of socialism with Chinese characteristics, giving fresh momentum to reform and opening up by laying out a clear path for regional integration.
Chinese President Xi Jinping takes in the view of Shenzhen at Lianhuashan Park, Guangdong Province, China, October 14, 2020. /Xinhua
2020 visit: 40th anniversary of SEZ
During his third visit in 2020, Xi returned to Shenzhen to attend a grand gathering marking the 40th anniversary of the establishment of the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone (SEZ).
The occasion came at a critical juncture in China's development, as the country faced mounting domestic and external economic pressures. Yet its stance on reform and opening up remained firm.
Addressing the gathering, Xi said, "The world economy is currently facing complicated challenges. By no means should we be stopped by the reversing trends and tides. We should choose the right side of the history to unswervingly expand opening-up in an all-round way, and promote the building of an open world economy and the building of a community with a shared future for humanity."
China's resolve in implementing reform and opening up has yielded significant results over the years. In the first three quarters of 2026, Shenzhen's GDP exceeded 3.02 trillion yuan, marking a 6.0% year-on-year increase at constant prices, an achievement that would not have been possible without the choices made decades ago.
Hailing the policy as the key to China's astonishing development during his 2021 speech marking the Communist Party of China's (CPC) centenary, Xi stressed that reform and opening up was a crucial move in making China what it is today, demonstrating once again the Party's commitment to the policy and its steady leadership.
In November 1991, China officially joined APEC, marking a major milestone in its reform and opening up policy by deepening its integration into the regional economy and expanding multilateral trade.
Thirty-five years later, China is bringing APEC to Shenzhen, the very place where its nationwide opening up to the world began. Coming full circle, China is once again rolling out the red carpet for the world.

item.title: How China is rebuilding 3,000-year-old bronze treasures
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
How do you put ancient treasures back together after thousands of years? At China's Sanxingdui archaeological site, conservators combine meticulous hands-on restoration with 3D scanning and digital modeling to study broken bronze artifacts and help reveal the extraordinary craftsmanship of ancient Shu civilization.
